subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 9
placeName: Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory

points.title: The real number system
points.brief: Real numbers are all the rational numbers (integers, fractions and terminating or recurring decimals) together with the irrational numbers, such as √5 and π.

points.title: Significant figures
points.brief: Rounding to significant figures counts from the first non-zero digit, so 0.004 562 to 2 significant figures is 0.0046.

points.title: Scientific notation for large numbers
points.brief: A large number is written as a number from 1 to less than 10 times a positive power of 10, so 3 400 000 = 3.4 × 10⁶.

points.title: Scientific notation for small numbers
points.brief: A small number uses a negative power of 10, so 0.000 52 = 5.2 × 10⁻⁴, as in the width of a cell in metres.

points.title: Index laws with variables
points.brief: The index laws work with variables too, so x⁵ × x³ = x⁸, x⁶ ÷ x² = x⁴ and (x²)³ = x⁶, with numbers in front multiplied or divided as usual.

points.title: Negative indices
points.brief: A negative index means a reciprocal, so 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8.

points.title: Expanding binomial products
points.brief: Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second, so (x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 8x + 15.

points.title: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
points.brief: Two special expansions, (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², save time.

points.title: Factorising monic quadratics
points.brief: To factorise x² + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b, so x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4).

points.title: Gradient of an interval
points.brief: Gradient is rise over run, the change in y divided by the change in x between two points, and it is negative when a line slopes down to the right.

points.title: Midpoint of an interval
points.brief: The midpoint is found by averaging the x-values and averaging the y-values of the two end points.

points.title: Distance between two points
points.brief: The distance between two points comes from Pythagoras' theorem, using the change in x and the change in y as the two shorter sides.

points.title: Gradient and y-intercept
points.brief: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is where the line cuts the y-axis, so changing m tilts the line and changing c shifts it up or down.

points.title: Graphing parabolas
points.brief: The graph of y = x² is a U-shaped parabola with its turning point at the origin and the y-axis as its line of symmetry.

points.title: Changing a parabola
points.brief: In y = ax², a larger a makes the parabola narrower and a negative a turns it upside down, while adding a number shifts it up or down.

points.title: Solving quadratics by factorising
points.brief: Factorise, then set each factor to zero, so x² − 5x + 6 = 0 becomes (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 and x = 2 or x = 3.

points.title: Solving quadratics from a graph
points.brief: The solutions of a quadratic equation equal to zero are the x-values where its parabola crosses the x-axis.

points.title: Choosing a linear or quadratic model
points.brief: Change by the same amount each step suits a linear model, while a path that rises then falls, such as a thrown ball, suits a quadratic one.

points.title: Surface area of prisms
points.brief: The surface area of a prism is the total area of all its faces, found by adding the area of each face, often using its net.

points.title: Volume of cylinders
points.brief: A cylinder's volume is the area of its circular base times its height, V = πr²h.

points.title: Surface area of cylinders
points.brief: A closed cylinder's surface area is two circles plus a curved surface that unrolls into a rectangle, giving SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

points.title: The trigonometric ratios
points.brief: In a right-angled triangle, sine is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse and tangent is opposite over adjacent, and similar triangles give the same ratios for the same angle.

points.title: Finding a side with trigonometry
points.brief: Choose the ratio that links the known angle, the known side and the unknown side, then rearrange, such as x = 10 × sin 30° = 5.

points.title: Finding an angle with trigonometry
points.brief: When two sides are known, find their ratio and use the inverse function on a calculator, such as tan⁻¹, to get the angle.

points.title: Direct proportion and scale
points.brief: Two quantities are in direct proportion when one is always the same multiple of the other, as in a scale drawing where 1 cm stands for 2 m.

points.title: Absolute, relative and percentage error
points.brief: Every measurement is an estimate. Absolute error is the gap between a measured and an actual value, relative error is that gap divided by the actual value, and percentage error is relative error times 100.

points.title: Enlargements
points.brief: An enlargement multiplies every distance from a centre by the same scale factor, so the image is the same shape but a different size.

points.title: What changes in an enlargement
points.brief: An enlargement keeps angles the same but multiplies lengths by the scale factor k, and multiplies area by k².

points.title: Finding sides in similar triangles
points.brief: Matching sides of similar triangles are in the same ratio, so an unknown side is found from the scale factor.

points.title: Geometric constructions as steps
points.brief: A construction, such as bisecting an angle with a compass and ruler, is an ordered set of steps, like an algorithm, that always works.

points.title: Reading survey reports critically
points.brief: Before trusting a survey's estimate of a mean or median, check who was asked, how many, and how the data was collected.

points.title: Sampling methods and bias
points.brief: Sampling methods such as random, systematic and stratified samples suit different situations, and a poor method, such as an online poll, can bias results.

points.title: Misleading graphs
points.brief: A graph can mislead with a vertical axis that does not start at zero, uneven scales or pictures sized wrongly, which pushes a point of view.

points.title: Comparing data sets
points.brief: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots and parallel dot plots put two data sets side by side to compare centre, spread, shape and outliers.

points.title: Choosing a display
points.brief: Categorical data suits a bar or pie chart, numerical data suits a histogram or dot plot, and change over time suits a line graph.

points.title: With and without replacement
points.brief: When an item is replaced, the probabilities stay the same for the next pick. When it is not replaced, the total and the counts change.

points.title: Listing outcomes for compound events
points.brief: Arrays, tables and tree diagrams list every outcome of a two- or three-step experiment, such as tossing three coins, so each probability can be found.

points.title: And, inclusive or and exclusive or
points.brief: A and B means both happen, inclusive A or B means either or both, and exclusive A or B means one but not both.

points.title: Estimating probability from relative frequency
points.brief: When outcomes are not equally likely, the relative frequency from many trials or past data estimates the probability.
